english.title: Master of ship involved in collision fail to give name of ship and destination/embarkation port to other master
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the master of a ship, namely **(..SPECIFY SHIP..), involved in a collision with another ship, namely **(..SPECIFY OTHER SHIP..), failed, without reasonable excuse, in so far as you could do without danger to your own ship, crew and passengers, to give to the master of the other ship the name of your own ship and also the names of the ports from which it came and to which it was bound
english.legislation: Contrary to section 92(1)(b) and (4)(b) of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: If the master is a certified officer, an enquiry into his conduct may be held, and his certificate cancelled or suspended - section 92(4)
